title: I Used the Ice-Rink Helmet Policy on the Parent Who Wrote the Waiver

parts.text: I laced my skates at 5:40 p.m. for public session and watched a dad put his kid on the ice without a helmet. The waiver on the clipboard, drafted by that same dad when he sat on the rink board, required helmets under twelve. I was thirty-one, skate guard, holding a stack of loaner lids. He said his kid was advanced. Advanced is not a waiver line. I photographed the clipboard signature block with his name and the kid's bare head from the penalty box camera we use for collisions. Then I blew the whistle. At 5:46 he filmed me and said I was targeting board families.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He is filming a skate guard while the penalty-box camera already has the bare head.

social.video_title: The waiver author skipped the helmet — Part 1/2
social.description: Public session, loaner lids, a board dad. The box camera was rolling. Would you have blown the whistle?

parts.text: Management backed the clipboard. The kid wore a loaner. The dad's video never posted because the rink's policy also banned filming staff, another paragraph he had written. He resigned from the board by email that used the word overreach. Overreach is a helmet. I stacked the loaners. Public session stayed public. Advanced kids still have skulls. The waiver did not get a family exception. It got a dad on the bench.

social.video_title: He had also banned filming staff — Part 2/2
social.description: Loaner lid, unposted video, a resignation email. Was advanced a paragraph?
